vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-chronicle
Version: 0.7.0

The Agent Chronicle skill is a comprehensive and well-structured journaling tool designed for AI agents to maintain a personal diary. It gathers context from local session logs and persistent memory files to generate reflective journal entries, which are stored locally within the agent's workspace. The bundle includes scripts for mood analytics (analyze.py), weekly digests (digest.py), and high-quality PDF/HTML exports (export.py, export_pdf.py). The implementation follows OpenClaw's recommended patterns, such as using sessions_spawn for sub-agent tasks, and shows no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized remote execution, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: Agent Chronicle's code, CLI scripts, and runtime instructions are coherent with a local diary/generation tool: it only needs python3, reads/writes diary files in the agent workspace, and uses OpenClaw sub-agent spawning for generation — there are no hidden network endpoints or credential requests in the package.

dimensions.detail: The skill is a diary/analytics/export tool and its files, CLI flags, and declared requirements (python3, optional pandoc/weasyprint) match that purpose. The use of sessions_spawn (OpenClaw-native) to run sub-agents is consistent with the described generation workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Scripts read and write files under a workspace 'memory/diary/' and can append diary summaries into the agent's main memory (memory_integration). The skill emits sub-agent tasks (sessions_spawn) that will send diary context to whatever model the platform runs — so diary contents could be processed by a hosted model. The SKILL.md notes an automatic first-run setup which will create files and directories; this behavior is expected but worth reviewing before first run.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only with included scripts). Dependencies are native binaries or Python libraries (pandoc, weasyprint, python-markdown) that are installed separately. The code does call subprocesses (pandoc) and imports third‑party Python libraries but does not download or execute arbitrary remote archives.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request secrets or external credentials. It looks for OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE or AGENT_WORKSPACE to locate the agent workspace — these environment variables are relevant to finding diary files. No unrelated env vars or keys are required.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true. The skill creates and modifies files under the agent workspace (diary files, exports) which is expected for its function. It does not claim to modify other skills or system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to do what it says, but review these items before enabling: 1) First-run setup is automatic when you run generate.py and will create diary files in your agent workspace — inspect config.json and choose diary_path you control. 2) If memory_integration is enabled the skill may append diary summaries to your agent's main memory; disable that option if entries may contain sensitive data. 3) The skill emits tasks for sub-agents (sessions_spawn) so diary contents will be sent to whatever model/runtime the platform uses — treat entries as data that could leave local context and review policies for model logging/retention. 4) Exports rely on external tools (pandoc, weasyprint, texlive) which run subprocesses; install them from trusted sources. 5) If you need absolute assurance, inspect scripts/generate.py and any code paths that build the sub-agent prompt/context before running the skill.
